anchorData: EARTH TURNING: Earth completes one full rotation (360°) about its axis in 24 hours (we use 24 h, not 23 h 56 min). Rate = 360° ÷ 24 h = 15° per hour. Earth turns anticlockwise when viewed from above the North Pole (west to east), so the Sun appears to move east to west. Nairobi is at about 36.8° E, Mombasa about 39.7° E, Kisumu about 34.8° E. Longitude differences: Mombasa minus Nairobi = 39.7 - 36.8 = 2.9°; Nairobi minus Kisumu = 36.8 - 34.8 = 2.0°; Mombasa minus Kisumu = 39.7 - 34.8 = 4.9°. Time for Earth to turn: 2.9° ÷ 15 = about 0.19 h, about 12 min; 2.0° ÷ 15 = about 0.13 h, about 8 min; 4.9° ÷ 15 = about 0.33 h, about 20 min. So Mombasa sees sunrise about 20 minutes before Kisumu (rounded, an east-ahead order: Mombasa first, then Nairobi, then Kisumu). Video snapshot times (East Africa Time, EAT): dawn Mombasa about 6:30 am; midday Nairobi about 12:30 pm; sunset Lake Victoria about 6:40 pm; darkness over Kisumu about 7:30 pm. Time-lapse: 24 h of Earth time shown in 24 seconds, so 1 second = 1 hour = 15° of turning. Classroom globe model: a globe tilted about 23.5° with a torch as the Sun; globe is turned anticlockwise (viewed from above the North Pole) through 15° for each hour. Angle facts: full turn 360°, half turn 180°, quarter turn 90°. Clock hand (minute hand) turns 360° per 60 min = 6° per minute; hour hand turns 360° per 12 h = 30° per hour. Rotational symmetry orders (all fixed): square 4 (angle 90°), equilateral triangle 3 (120°), regular hexagon 6 (60°), rectangle (non-square) 2 (180°), regular pentagon 5 (72°), isosceles non-equilateral triangle 1, kiondo (sisal basket) star-pattern base: 6 (60°), bicycle wheel with 8 equally spaced spokes: 8 (45°), matatu wheel with 5 nuts: 5 (72°). Solids: cuboid (non-square ends) has 3 axes each of order 2; square-based prism (square cross-section, length different) has one axis of order 4 and two axes of order 2 (through opposite face centres); cone has 1 axis of order infinity (every angle); cube has 3 axes of order 4, 4 axes of order 3, 6 axes of order 2 (13 total, may be mentioned only as an extension); Earth/globe axis: one axis through the North and South Poles, order infinity as a sphere. Cartesian plane worked example: centre O(0,0), A(2,1) rotated 90° anticlockwise gives A'(-1,2); B(4,1) gives B'(-1,4); C(4,3) gives C'(-3,4). Check: rule (x,y) goes to (-y,x). Distances: OA = OA' = square root of 5; OB = OB' = square root of 17; OC = OC' = 5. Triangle ABC: AB = 2, BC = 2, AC = square root of 8 and A'B'=2, B'C'=2, A'C'=square root of 8 (image congruent). Negative angle: -90° means 90° clockwise; A(2,1) rotated -90° gives A''(1,-2) by rule (x,y) goes to (y,-x). Half turn about O: (x,y) goes to (-x,-y). Locating centre example: P(1,1) to P'(1,5) and Q(3,1) to Q'(1,3) with centre C(1,3)? NOT used. Use instead: P(2,0)→P'(0,2) and Q(4,0)→Q'(0,4) with centre O(0,0), angle 90° anticlockwise (rule check: (2,0)→(0,2), (4,0)→(0,4)); perpendicular bisector of PP' is the line y = x, of QQ' is the line y = x, so use a third pair R(3,2)→R'(-2,3) whose perpendicular bisector is y = -x/... only state the centre as O(0,0) found where bisectors of PP' and RR' meet.
characters: Learners in a Grade 10 class in Nairobi use a globe, torch, tracing paper and grid paper. Wanjiku: a Grade 10 learner in Kisumu who sees the Sun set over Lake Victoria; she says 'Kenya feels still'. Otieno: a learner at Mombasa who sees dawn first over the Indian Ocean. Teacher Mwangi: guides the class. Mombasa: east coast, sunrise earliest of the three cities (about 20 min before Kisumu). Nairobi: central, on the equator side (about 1° S), midday sun about 12:30 pm. Kisumu: west, on Lake Victoria, sunrise latest of the three. Mama Achieng: a Kisumu basket weaver who makes kiondo/sisal patterns with 6-fold symmetry. Mzee Kamau: a Nairobi bicycle mechanic with an 8-spoke wheel. Wind turbines at Lake Turkana Wind Power (Marsabit County): 3 blades each, order of rotational symmetry 3 (120°). Kenya is not stationary: it turns with Earth. The DQB is the Driving Question Board kept on a wall chart.
outcome: Day and night repeat every 24 hours because Earth rotates once (360°) about its axis in 24 hours, turning anticlockwise at 15° per hour as seen from above the North Pole, while the Sun's light always lights one half. Places further east, like Mombasa, turn into the sunlight sooner than places further west like Kisumu, so Mombasa gets sunrise about 20 minutes earlier. The Sun only appears to move east to west; the turning is described with a centre (Earth's axis), an angle (15° per hour) and a direction (anticlockwise).
conventions: Rotation is described by three things: centre, angle, direction. Positive angle = anticlockwise; negative angle = clockwise (so -90° means 90° clockwise). Angles in degrees (°). Object = original figure; image = result, named with a dash (A to A'). Centre of rotation is found by perpendicular bisectors of object-image point pairs (at least two pairs). Rotation is a direct isometry: preserves lengths, angles, size, shape, and orientation of turn is changed only in direction of facing; object and image are directly congruent. Order of rotational symmetry = number of times a figure fits onto itself in one full turn of 360°; the smallest angle of fit = 360° ÷ order. A figure with order 1 has no rotational symmetry. Axis of rotational symmetry (solids) is a line through the solid about which it fits onto itself; state its order. Use East Africa Time (EAT) for times. Use 15° per hour and 24 h as exact. Rounded times are given to the nearest minute as above. Use the word 'rotation', not 'revolution', for Earth's spin on its axis.
